ranking.note: Raised to P1: release-binary verification tooling counting revoked/expired keys toward the quorum is a disclosed security defect in a tool downstream users rely on, the most consequential problem in this category.

Raised to P2 and moved up: the wrapper is simply unusable on distros with non-default libexec layout (issue #35785), the same class of supported-platform breakage as #36105, so the two must share a band.
Raised to P2: the problem is recurring privacy/deanonymization leaks in private broadcast, a security-class issue, not merely a new CLI utility.
Raised to P2 and moved up: substantial snapshot-load performance gain plus an offline bitcoin-util inspection tool, and #35054 (P2P UTXO set sharing) builds on it.
Raised from P4: silently swallowing options after a command (e.g. trailing -rpcwallet) is a real user-facing CLI correctness problem, not incidental cleanup.
Moved down: a useful developer/researcher convenience tool with no existing breakage behind it, so it ranks below the tool bugs and the dev-time-saving automation in the same band.
Moved down: maintainability of a developer dependency check with unresolved design-doc objections and a stale branch ranks below concrete tool bugs and user-facing tooling in the same band.

inconsistencies: Chain: #36105 (Windows exec/_cwait fix) must be reviewed before #36190, which only adds functional tests for the behaviour #36105 introduces; reviewing the tests first is wasted effort.
Chain: #19460 depends on #10102 and #29409 and is itself a prerequisite for #19461; its value is entirely as scaffolding, so it should be reviewed in that sequence rather than on its own merits.

#35814 supersedes the earlier stalled completion-generation attempts (#18606, #25243, #30860) and builds on merged OpenRPC work (#34683) — it is the one to review for issue #17289; the older PRs should be closed rather than re-reviewed.

#36603 and #36608 both land new binaries/subcommands in the tools surface while the bulk of their diffs sit in node and P2P code; reviewers from this category should focus on the bitcoin-util txoutsetsummary and bitcoin-privbcast interfaces and defer the rest.

#35994 is a draft whose author has stated a preference for abandoning it in favour of manual rewrites; it is kept at P4 rather than Unranked because intent is clear, but it has no claim on review time.
result.notes: Band spread is deliberate: one P1 (security defect in release verification), four P2s (two concrete supported-platform/distro failures of the `bitcoin` wrapper, one privacy rewrite, one perf+unblocking change), with the rest genuine but deferrable developer and contrib tooling. Several cards' stated reasons under-described their PRs (notably #36106, #36603, #35831), which is where the bands moved.
